# x86_avx.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/avx-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 7763 (raven-macos-bench run 44501136642, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 40a755f6ffa80c9164b2b0069bd94de0bf77bd9040d406b137835bb05f26340e): the tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change.
# Earlier runs: an AMD EPYC 9V74 (run 44499294363) gave the same results for the families it had. An Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C (run 44500206597, dump sha256 37b9cf0cca10f7637359a6b9f4038e75c67ac913423a83c8aff9da653fdcdcf8) agrees with Rosetta in the strings family, as the EPYC does, and differs from the AMD runs in one dpps case (#7786, NaN lanes), not applied here: the AMD EPYC stays the reference.
